slides.title: Debrief: structure-function reasoning

cards.title: fallopian tubes
cards.body: fertilization usually occurs before the conceptus reaches the uterus.

cards.title: uterus

cards.title: ovaries
cards.body: ovarian and menstrual cycle timing helps estimate ovulation and gestational age.

cards.title: cervical/vaginal/external structures

slides.title: Checkpoint: choose the best explanation
slides.question: A patient asks, 'Why does my cycle date matter if I already have a positive pregnancy test?' Best nursing response?
options: Cycle dates are only used for infertility, not pregnancy.
Cycle dates help estimate timing, but symptoms and prenatal follow-up still matter.
The exact conception day can always be calculated from the positive test.
You do not need to discuss cycle dates once pregnancy is confirmed.
slides.rationale: cycle timing supports estimation, but does not replace assessment and follow-up.

slides.title: Mini case: respond to Maya without guessing
slides.scenario: Maya says, 'I took ibuprofen twice and had alcohol before I knew. I feel okay today. Plus, I had light spotting yesterday.'

steps.title: 1. assess first
steps.body: bleeding amount, pain, dizziness, fever, LMP, medication dose, exposure details

steps.title: 2. teach clearly
steps.body: stop avoidable exposures now; review meds with prenatal provider; keep follow-up

steps.title: 3. avoid false certainty
steps.body: do not promise no risk; do not create panic; focus on urgent cues and next steps

slides.title: Practice: patient teaching script

steps.title: acknowledge
steps.body: I hear that you are worried.

steps.title: assess safety
steps.body: ask targeted symptom and exposure questions.

steps.title: explain simply

steps.title: reduce risk
steps.body: avoid preventable exposures and know urgent symptoms.

slides.title: Genetic basics: know your nursing lane

cards.title: what students should know
cards.body: chromosomes carry genetic information; inheritance patterns can affect screening and risk discussion

cards.title: what nurses assess
cards.body: family history, pregnancy history, congenital concerns, screening questions, patient understanding

cards.title: what nurses do not overclaim
cards.body: do not provide genetic counseling beyond scope; refer to genetics resources when appropriate

cards.title: what nurses teach
cards.body: plain language, consent, limits of screening, and follow-up

slides.learner_task: separate basic knowledge from nursing scope and referral needs

slides.title: Capstone scenario: choose the next safe action
slides.scenario: Maya calls back: 'The spotting is heavier. I have sharp pain on one side and I almost fainted in the bathroom.'
slides.question: What is the priority nursing response?
options: Explain that spotting can be normal and schedule routine teaching.
Ask her to track symptoms for 24 hours and call back if they continue.
Recognize urgent cues, assess immediate safety, and direct urgent evaluation/escalation per protocol.
Begin a detailed explanation of fetal development to reduce anxiety.
slides.rationale: heavier bleeding, unilateral sharp pain, and near-syncope are urgent cues requiring escalation, not reassurance alone.
slides.learner_task: choose the safest next action and justify it

slides.title: Capstone debrief: why C is safest

cards.title: recognize cues
cards.body: heavier bleeding, sharp unilateral pain, near-syncope are not routine teaching cues.

cards.title: analyze risk
cards.body: early pregnancy complication is possible; maternal safety comes first.

cards.title: take action
cards.body: escalate according to protocol and direct urgent evaluation; do not reassure without assessment.

slides.title: Chapter 2 takeaway: biology becomes nursing action

actions.title: teach
actions.body: use plain language for timing, anatomy, implantation, and fetal support

actions.title: assess
actions.body: ask about history, symptoms, medications, exposures, and risk factors

actions.title: escalate
actions.body: prioritize bleeding, severe pain, syncope, fever, and abnormal cues

actions.title: reassure
actions.body: only after understanding, context, and red flags are ruled out

slides.statement: A safe nurse can explain the process, reduce preventable risk, screen for urgent cues, and connect the patient to timely follow-up.
slides.learner_task: state one bedside action for each frame
